_comment: The single source of truth for the IndieOps Skilllet catalogue, published from the public indieops-co/skilllet-registry repo. Every guide's chooser is generated from this file at build time, and every downloaded guide quietly re-reads it (catalogueUrls, first that answers wins) to show anything released since.

brand.name: IndieOps
brand.signature: An IndieOps Skilllet — a copyable skill folder that does one job properly.
brand.termNote: Skilllet, three Ls. It is our word. Spelling it consistently is the cheapest brand asset we own.

_idRule: id is assigned once, at first public release, and never changes. Format: <release year>-<sequence within that year>. The version carries freshness; the id is a primary key. Re-stamping an id because something was revised destroys the only property that makes it an id. One sequence covers skilllets, software, courses and reserved: the next free id is one past the highest in all four lists.

_kindValues.skill: Copy a folder next to your work.
_kindValues.plugin: Install from a Claude Code plugin marketplace.
_kindValues.app: Also installs a program that runs on your computer (a background service or a desktop app).

_urlRule: A card links to the entry's url if it has one (https only), otherwise to <brand.productPages>/<slug> (indieops.co/skills/<slug>, so the top level stays free for marketing pages). 'previously' lists retired slugs so the site can redirect them.
_repoRule: repo is the GitHub repo (and local folder) name inside indieops-co. It can differ from slug: slug is the product's identity (the shipped folder, the SKILL.md name, the /command, the Shared Profiles notes file, the indieops.co page) and never changes; the repo name is just where the code is stored.
_priceRule: Skilllet prices live here and nowhere else (software is priced on the site; see _softwareRule): price is the current price in whole US dollars, 0 for free. The indieops.co catalogue page and the store read it from here, so changing a price is one edit. Nothing shipped to a buyer (guides, covers, READMEs, licenses) ever shows a price, because a price inside a downloaded file can't be changed; build-guide refuses a chooser that contains one. Marketing drafts write {{price}} and fill it in on the day. An entry with no price field isn't priced yet. freeTier names a free edition of a paid Skilllet (PromptAwesome Core); price is then the paid edition's. The price also picks the license: 0 ships the IndieOps Free License, anything else the IndieOps Commercial License, and a freeTier edition ships the Free one.
_billingRule: A Skilllet is a single payment, so a skilllets entry carries no billing or usage field: every guide's chooser tells the reader 'no subscription', and guides already downloaded keep saying it. Anything sold by the year is software and goes in the software list.
_checkoutRule: checkout is the entry's Lemon Squeezy checkout link, https only. A product page's download button goes through it even when price is 0, so every download leaves the email that updates are sent to. Empty means the store product isn't set up yet, and the page says the download opens soon. Only the indieops.co product pages read it; it is never shown in anything that ships. An entry that is still building keeps it empty until it ships.
_platformRule: platforms, worksWith and needs are what a cover page's platform line shows. Set them here first and copy them to the cover, so the two can't disagree. platforms: macos | windows | linux, each the minimum OS version ('' when there is none worth stating). worksWith: the AI assistants it has been tested with: claude | codex | gemini. Only list what has passed a real run; add one later in a new version. needs: other software with its minimum version, in the words the cover uses.
_softwareRule: software lists IndieOps Software that has an id: tools sold as a yearly subscription (and included for IndieOps Business Incubator members), not Skilllets. They take ids from the same sequence so nothing can collide, but they live in their own list because every guide's chooser, including the live top-up inside guides already downloaded, reads only skilllets and promises no subscription. Their price, billing, usage line, checkout and homepage line live in the indieops.co site's src/data/products.json with the rest of the software, so a price is still kept in one place. Fields: id, slug, name, status (shipped | building | planned), problem, does, repo.
_courseRule: courses are IndieOps Courses: single-file HTML courses, delivered as $0 Lemon Squeezy lead magnets and listed on indieops.co/guides. They take ids from the same sequence as skilllets so the two can never collide, but they live in their own list because the guides' choosers and the indieops.co directory read only skilllets: a course never appears as a card under 'Which Skilllet do you need next?'. Fields: id, slug, name, series, status (shipped | building), problem, does, and source (its folder in the private guides repo).
_reservedRule: reserved holds an id claimed by a Skilllet whose entry is still waiting in a pull request (one that merges on release day). Nothing reads it except whoever picks the next id. The pull request that adds the entry to skilllets deletes its line here.

skilllets.name: TastePilot
skilllets.problem: Your writing is good and it looks like a text file.
skilllets.does: Renders Markdown into designed HTML publications using Canons — swappable design grammars.
needs: bash for setup (Git Bash or WSL on Windows)

skilllets.name: OAuth Coach
skilllets.problem: Your Google sign-in screen says "some-project-84f2b" and nobody trusts it.
skilllets.does: Diagnoses and polishes Google OAuth consent branding for Supabase and Firebase apps.

skilllets.name: Resend Ready
skilllets.problem: Your app needs to send email and you have never configured a sending domain.
skilllets.does: Takes a Next.js app from no email to sending — and optionally receiving — through Resend, with DNS verified.

skilllets.name: Press Ready
skilllets.problem: You are about to publish files carrying invisible characters and metadata you did not mean to send.
skilllets.does: Lossless pre-publish hygiene — invisible Unicode, file metadata, C2PA, whole folders at a time.
needs: exiftool, qpdf and ffmpeg for some file types (optional)

skilllets.name: Instantly Ready
skilllets.problem: Cold email infrastructure has nine moving parts and getting one wrong burns the domain.
skilllets.does: Walks a beginner from signup to a verified READY TO SEND state, with a bundled DNS checker.

skilllets.name: Claujabi
skilllets.problem: Course platforms want a monthly fee to host a thing you already made.
skilllets.does: Turns an outline or a pasted transcript into a distributable single-file HTML course with progress saved.
needs: Chrome, Edge or Brave for PDF export

skilllets.name: Flipbook Maker
skilllets.problem: A long document nobody finishes reading.
skilllets.does: Converts text, markdown, a PDF, a post or a transcript into a self-contained interactive HTML flipbook.

skilllets.name: ApprovalPilot
skilllets.problem: A good plan-mode session dies when the context window does.
skilllets.does: At the plan-approval moment it shows how full your context is, says whether to hand off, and puts a complete handoff prompt on your clipboard.

skilllets.name: Reminder Router
skilllets.problem: Four AI sessions running and no idea which one needs you.
skilllets.does: A context-aware handoff utility that routes your attention to the project that actually stalled.

skilllets.name: StoryBook Cover
skilllets.problem: The story is written and the cover looks like clip art.
skilllets.does: Turns a story title and a few details into image prompts that produce one coherent storybook cover.
needs: Any image generator (Midjourney, GPT Image, Flux…)

skilllets.name: Memvana
skilllets.problem: Four thousand screenshots and a Notes app you have not opened in a year.
skilllets.does: Reads the pile and works out what you were actually trying to remember.

skilllets.name: LinkPanther
skilllets.problem: Your links are on somebody else's domain and you cannot change where they point.
skilllets.does: Works out the most branded URL architecture your domain can safely support, then builds and runs it.

skilllets.name: GBPCoach
skilllets.problem: Google Maps decides whether a local business gets called, and nobody explains how.
skilllets.does: Learns a business once, grades its Google Business Profile, and hands over three things to do this week with the copy already written.

skilllets.name: GBPCoach Pro
skilllets.problem: You can see your own profile. You cannot see what the businesses beating you have done.
skilllets.does: Adds live Maps data via your own API key — category intelligence, competitor files, review benchmarking, a client-ready monthly report.

skilllets.name: Shared Profiles
skilllets.problem: Our other Skilllets reference this for your and your clients' profiles & preferences.
skilllets.does: One folder of plain notes on your computer, your profile and one per business, that every IndieOps Skilllet reads and writes. Install it once and they stop asking.

skilllets.name: CaveMaxx
skilllets.problem: You asked a question and got an essay when a diagram would have done.
skilllets.does: Teaches Claude to notice when a chart, calculator, comparison or mini-app would serve you better than prose, and to build that instead.
needs: Claude Code, or a Claude plan with custom skills

skilllets.name: Pilot-Pilot
skilllets.problem: Your script reads like everybody else's AI script.
skilllets.does: An AI writer's room: learns your voice, develops the story, writes for the format, then hunts down the AI slop before your audience does.
needs: Python 3.9+ for lint and PDF export (optional)

skilllets.name: QuestionPilot
skilllets.problem: Claude Code asks a question and the picker grabs your terminal before you've had a chance to think.
skilllets.does: Catches Claude Code's questions first, so you can read them, copy them, and decide what happens next.

skilllets.name: PromptAwesome
skilllets.problem: Every AI tool wants its prompts shaped differently, and yours are scattered across notes apps.
skilllets.does: A prompt library that lives in your repo. It asks the few questions that change the output, shapes the prompt for the tool you're pasting into, and keeps every version.

skilllets.name: LaunchSkeptic
skilllets.problem: You're about to spend months building an idea nobody has checked.
skilllets.does: Researches the idea and returns pursue, pivot or kill, with every claim sourced and a 14-day plan to prove it wrong.
needs: Web search turned on in Claude

skilllets.name: ruv lite
skilllets.problem: Everyone's talking about Ruflo, RuVector and agent swarms, and you can't tell which of it your project actually needs.
skilllets.does: Weighs the simple option against the rUv one and says use it, later or skip it, with the cost, the trigger to revisit and current sources.
needs: Web search turned on in Claude, for live source checks (optional)

software.name: GBP Magnet
software.problem: Local businesses are losing calls to a weak Google Business Profile, and you can't find them fast enough to help.
software.does: Finds local businesses whose Google Business Profile is costing them calls, and hands you the opening line.

courses.name: Turn Strangers Into Regulars
courses.problem: I keep launching to an empty room.
courses.does: Eight short Issues and a 30-day build that set up a small, honest marketing system: a page before launch, a list you own, a three-email welcome and numbers that help you decide.

reserved.name: Cabinet-Ready
reserved.note: Its entry waits in skilllet-registry PR #3, which merges on release day and deletes this line.
